Detailed method

10 short logs come from this batch. Currently 500 g flour, 62% hydration, 2% salt, and 1.1% yeast. That is 310 g water, 10 g salt, and 5.5 g yeast, 825.5 g of dough. Currently 10 logs of 82.6 g. Proof them touching so the sides stay pale. Slash the top before baking so a sausage has an opening. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 310 g water, 10 g salt, and 5.5 g instant yeast, then knead about 8 minutes until smooth. At 62% the dough is soft and holds a ball. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 80 minutes. With 1.1% yeast it should about double.
  3. Divide Divide the 825.5 g dough into 10 pieces of 82.6 g, the weight in the balls fields. Cover and rest 10 minutes.
  4. Shape Roll each piece into a log about 15 cm long. Set the logs in one row on a sheet, touching, seam-side down. The default 825.5 g uses a baking sheet about 40 cm long and 30 cm wide. If you change the amount, use a sheet sized to fit, or bake in batches.
  5. Proof Cover them for 30 to 45 minutes, until they look puffy. Keep them touching so the sides that meet stay pale.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Slash each log once along the top, about 1 cm deep, so the sausage has an opening. Bake 14 to 18 minutes, until the tops are golden.
  7. Cool Set them on a rack for at least 20 minutes. Set a sausage in that slash.
